Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — cost-aware, correctness-gated A/B harness (the ecosystem benchmark of the author's open-source vigiles auditor) applied to two token-efficiency tools vs a no-tool baseline in Claude Code on Claude Sonnet: 7 tasks x 5 trials x 2 arms x 2 tools = 140 runs

Two third-party token-efficiency tools for Claude Code: 'caveman' skill (commit f06348c, fetched 2026-06-20; plugin with activation hook) and claude-token-efficient ('Token-Eff.', commit 0d30a6d, fetched 2026-06-21; project-memory file); compared with a no-tool baseline

caveman: a skill instructing terse, telegraphic answers, loaded through the agent's plugin mechanism with its own activation hook; it also has a feature that compresses an instructions file (shrank one by 68%). Token-Eff.: a compact project-memory file placed where the agent auto-loads it

Automatic: harness records all token classes charged by the API per run and prices them; deterministic structural checks on the produced artefact. Statistics: Welch t-test per task, Bonferroni within each tool, paired t-test on the 7 per-task cost differences with 95% CI

Criteria stated by the author: correctness gate (no regression vs the paired baseline) for quality; the tools' advertised savings (65% caveman, 63% Token-Eff.; 63-75% overall) as the claim tested for cost. 5 trials per task per arm, 7 tasks.
- No tool (baseline) + Claude Code + Claude Sonnet (alias 'sonnet', not pinned): all runs passed the checks; output ~0.6% of session tokens and ~20% of dollar cost (pooled). Quality verdict: works (gate passed); cost verdict: no criterion stated by the author (reference arm)
- caveman skill + Claude Code + Claude Sonnet: mean output change ~-6%; per-task output change slugify +54%, debounce -28%, bugfix -31% (p=0.002), bigO -18%, regex-email -28% (p=0.006), review-doc -8%, refactor-suite +21%; bill -1% pooled (+5% unweighted per-task), 95% CI [-21%, +31%], p~0.66, n=7; slugify arm ~70% more cached tokens and ~66% higher cost; compressing an instructions file by 68% gave no significant session saving; zero regressions. Quality verdict: works (no regressions on the shallow gate); cost verdict: does not work (advertised 65% not reached, bill flat)
- claude-token-efficient + Claude Code + Claude Sonnet: per-task output change -2%, -7%, -6%, +6%, +127% (regex-email, p=0.037, not significant after Bonferroni), +54%, +33%; bill +10%, 95% CI [-8%, +29%], p~0.22; zero regressions. Quality verdict: works (no regressions on the shallow gate); cost verdict: does not work (advertised 63% not reached, bill flat or higher)
- Pilot: no-tool runs on Claude Haiku (2 tasks x 2 trials): output 1.1% of session tokens; verdicts: no criterion stated by the author

Tasks: 7 author-written tasks with structural checks (Table 1). Configurations: baseline (no tool) vs tool installed as a user would, for 2 tools. Baseline: no tool, same agent and model. Held constant: agent (Claude Code), model alias 'sonnet' (build not pinned), tasks and checks; tools pinned to commits. Acceptance tests: deterministic structural checks (no code execution), regression vs paired baseline discards the run. Repetitions: 5 trials per task per arm (140 runs). Human intervention: Not stated

caveman: output cut ~6% on average (vs 65% advertised), two per-task cuts significant after Bonferroni (bugfix -31%, regex -28%); bill -1% pooled, not significant (CI [-21%, +31%]). Token-Eff.: bill +10%, not significant (CI [-8%, +29%]); its one significant per-task cell is a cost increase (+127%). CIs exclude savings near the advertised 63-75% but cannot resolve differences below ~13%. Output is ~20% of the bill, so even a perfect 65% output cut caps bill savings at ~13%

Detected per-task output cuts of 28-31% and a 66% cost penalty at n=5, but could not settle bill differences below ~13% (wide CIs, p-values read as descriptive). Gate never fired; it is shallow (no execution). Limitations stated: 5 trials per task; one model (Sonnet; Haiku pilot only); short tasks (<=10 turns); one harness; two tools; author-written tasks and checks; model alias not pinned; trial-level rows not released (only per-task aggregates). Equivalence test (TOST) on a larger corpus and longer sessions as future work

Limitations: scale (5 trials), one model, short tasks, single harness, no multi-agent systems, two tools and author-written tasks, shallow correctness gate; latency and rate limits not evaluated. Gaps: agent-tooling claims are produced under conditions that do not match deployment; evaluation should measure dollar cost on realistic multi-turn sessions with a correctness gate and faithful installation; future work: TOST equivalence test, longer sessions, stronger gate that runs the code, larger task corpus

Pooled bill -1% vs +5% unweighted per-task average for caveman, both reported (p. 3). Abstract says the bill 'does not move at all'; the CIs are wide ([-21%, +31%]). Harness, task and check definitions public (github.com/zernie/vigiles, bench/ecosystem/); per-task, per-arm aggregates released with a self-checking script; individual trial rows not released.
